question: What is the primary purpose of a Public-Private Partnership in healthcare?

options.A: Transferring all health sector control to private owners
options.B: Combining public obligations with private resources
options.C: Reducing the total number of available hospitals
options.D: Eliminating government oversight in medical facilities

explanation: PPPs merge government health responsibilities with private sector funding and management to improve health system capacity. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why do governments in resource-limited settings engage in healthcare partnerships?

options.A: To completely avoid paying healthcare workers salaries
options.B: To build infrastructure without immediate total funding
options.C: To bypass all existing national health regulations
options.D: To stop providing free care to emergency patients

explanation: These arrangements allow governments to acquire modern facilities and equipment by leveraging private capital. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h1)

question: What distinguishes outsourcing from privatization in the health sector?

options.A: Privatization uses only external volunteer workers
options.B: Outsourcing retains public ownership of the facility
options.D: Privatization always improves daily nursing workflows

explanation: Outsourcing delegates task execution while the government maintains ultimate ownership and accountability of the health facility. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h2)

question: The main reason a hospital decides to outsource a department is to:

options.A: Permanently eliminate all hospital administrative jobs
options.B: Stop following national clinical practice guidelines
options.C: Allow internal staff to focus on core clinical duties
options.D: Hand over complete legal liability to the vendor

explanation: Delegating auxiliary services frees up internal personnel to concentrate on direct patient care and primary medical operations. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h2)

question: In a Build-Operate-Transfer model, who eventually takes ownership of the facility?
explanation: After the private partner operates the facility for the agreed timeframe, ownership reverts to the public sector. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h3)

question: A private consortium handles design, construction, funding, and management under which model?
explanation: The DBFO acronym captures the complete lifecycle of responsibilities assigned to the private partner in that specific framework. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a non-clinical service typically outsourced by hospitals?
explanation: Laboratory testing is a clinical service involving direct diagnostic patient care, unlike laundry, security, and catering. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why do hospitals often outsource specialized clinical services like advanced imaging?

options.A: To access expensive technology without capital purchase
options.B: To comply with mandatory international isolation rules
options.C: To remove all nursing accountability from the ward
options.D: To eliminate the need for patient medical records

explanation: Outsourcing clinical specialties enables hospitals to leverage vendor equipment and expertise without buying expensive machines upfront. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h4)

question: What is a primary ethical conflict that arises when private companies run health services?

options.A: Private vendors refusing to hire qualified Nigerian nurses
options.B: Profit motives conflicting with equitable public health access
options.C: Government inability to ever inspect outsourced facilities
options.D: Mandatory elimination of all traditional hospital departments

explanation: Private entities seek financial returns, which can clash with the government's duty to provide affordable care to all citizens. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h5)

question: A major operational risk of poorly managed hospital outsourcing is:

options.A: Instantaneous elimination of all hospital administrative duties
options.B: Fragmented communication disrupting team care coordination
options.C: Permanent removal of medical legal liability from doctors
options.D: Automatic promotion of all junior nurses to management

explanation: When external vendors and internal staff do not communicate well, patient safety and workflow continuity suffer. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h5)

question: What tools do health managers use to monitor vendor performance in outsourced contracts?
explanation: KPIs provide measurable standards used to evaluate whether the private vendor is delivering services according to the contract. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why are strong regulatory frameworks necessary before signing healthcare partnership deals?

options.A: To protect public interests and ensure service quality
options.B: To prevent nurses from participating in hospital management
options.C: To remove the need for any ongoing government oversight
options.D: To guarantee that private vendors make maximum profits

explanation: Clear regulations establish boundaries and accountability mechanisms, safeguarding patients and public resources. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h6)

question: How should a ward nurse interact with staff from an outsourced cleaning company?

options.A: Ignore their daily presence since they are external workers
options.B: Take over their cleaning duties to save hospital money
options.C: Coordinate closely with them to maintain infection control
options.D: Report them directly to the national medical licensing board

explanation: Nurses must work collaboratively with all support personnel to ensure environmental hygiene and patient safety standards are met. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h7)

question: What key role do nurses play regarding outsourced services in a health facility?

options.A: Designing architectural layouts for new partnership buildings
options.B: Paying the monthly salaries of all external contractor staff
options.C: Acting as patient advocates to monitor care quality
options.D: Directly negotiating financial contracts with private vendors

explanation: Nurses observe the daily impact of outsourced services on patients and advocate for corrective actions when standards drop. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h7)
